public_rationale: An independent systematic evaluation found recurring harmful responses when attackers bypassed GPT-4's safeguards. That supports the ordinary reading that substantial control problems persisted. The same study found stronger resistance to some attacks and few harmful responses without jailbreaks. Those improvements qualify the rhetoric but do not refute persistence of the problem.
limitations: The evidence concerns adversarial prompting, not the frequency of harmful responses in ordinary use.
The study does not establish that GPT-4 was equally difficult to control as its predecessors.
The metaphor is interpreted behaviorally; it does not attribute intentions to the model.
The single-year event date avoids assigning all experiments to one day when a correction rerun occurred.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: GPT-4 will be reckless and hard to control like its predecessors.

statement.excerpt: GPT-4 will still, like its predecessors, be a bull in a china shop, reckless and hard to control.
statement.document_title: What to Expect When You’re Expecting … GPT-4

our_interpretation: The plain reading predicts recurring harmful or unwanted outputs despite efforts to constrain the model.
The surrounding sentences connect the metaphor to unreliable behavior and imperfect control.
Like its predecessors means retaining these problems, not necessarily having an equal or higher failure rate.
Repeated failures across a systematic adversarial evaluation qualify; an isolated anecdote would not.
criteria.support_condition: A systematic evaluation of released original-generation GPT-4 demonstrates recurring harmful responses or safety-control failures despite its safeguards.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, credible evaluations demonstrate dependable control across relevant ordinary and adversarial requests, incompatible with recurring substantial failures.

evidence.locator: Section 3.2, Example: Base64; sections 2.2 and 4 report evaluation methods and results; appendix C.1 gives collection dates
evidence.publisher: Alexander Wei, Nika Haghtalab, and Jacob Steinhardt / arXiv
evidence.explanation: The systematic evaluation documents repeated harmful outputs under jailbreaks; its main GPT data collection ran from April 26 through May 1, with a subsequent correction rerun. Material qualification within the same study is that unmodified requests rarely elicited harmful answers and some attacks were less effective against GPT-4 than GPT-3.5.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: The 2023 experiments, publicly reported on July 5, documented repeated harmful control failures in released GPT-4 across systematic jailbreak testing.
